bull_case: Growth in credentials, transactions and VAS deepens client wallet share and value delivered.
bear_case: Large clients have bargaining power and Visa pays substantial client incentives to secure routing/issuance relationships.
thesis: Customer value is exceptionally strong because Visa sits inside mission-critical payment flows and monetizes high recurring usage without funding consumer credit itself.

evidence.claim: Q3 payments volume +10%, processed transactions +10%, cross-border ex-Europe +12%.

counterevidence: Regulatory and interchange litigation can pressure network economics and pricing over time.
The current valuation already embeds a high-quality compounder profile.
unknowns: Long-run regulation of interchange and routing
Sustainable growth rate of Visa Direct and value-added services
falsifiers: If processed transactions and payments volume decelerate materially while client incentives rise faster than gross revenue, the moat/FCF thesis weakens.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Growth is supported by mission-critical network usage, not marketing/subsidy without customer value.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Visa has multiple client types, geographies and revenue pools; regulation is important but no single customer/product/regulation is a fatal dependency.

next_checks: Payments volume, cross-border volume, processed transactions, value-added services, client incentives, owner FCF/share, buyback price

subscores.rationale: Authorization, settlement, fraud/risk, tokenization and global acceptance are mission-critical infrastructure for issuers, acquirers and merchants.
Payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions all continue expanding at high-single/low-double-digit rates.
Visa's asset-light network produces very high operating cash flow with limited capex relative to revenue.

uncertainties.rationale: Regulation, incentives and valuation are the main uncertainty.
